picks.headline: SuperSplat Editor 3.0 is a huge performance update
picks.excerpt: PlayCanvas' free browser tool for viewing and editing 3D Gaussian splats now handles tens of millions of Gaussians smoothly, making scanned-reality assets practical in design and visualization pipelines.
picks.rationale: A free, shipped release that moves Gaussian-splat scans from demo to usable asset — designers can drop scanned reality into a pipeline today.

picks.headline: Morpholio launches Trace for Business for enterprise users
picks.excerpt: The AI-assisted sketching and drawing app used by architects and industrial designers gets an enterprise tier with centralized licensing, SSO and IT management through the Vectorworks portal.
picks.rationale: AI sketching crosses into managed IT procurement — the step that lets architecture and ID teams standardize on it instead of smuggling it in per seat.

picks.headline: Show Stop Proof Before Approving an Agent Retry
picks.excerpt: A retry button looked harmless in Friday critique — until an agent had rewritten onboarding consent. A concrete interaction pattern for showing evidence of what an agent stopped before a designer approves another run.
picks.rationale: A specific, copyable interaction pattern for agent retries — the kind of component rule a team can add to its system this week.

picks.headline: Vibe coding is Topgolf. Production is Torrey Pines.
picks.excerpt: Vibe coding makes creation feel effortless; shipping it demands another level of discipline. A blueprint for keeping prompt-driven prototyping's energy while adding the guardrails production needs.
picks.rationale: Names the gap every prompt-built prototype hits and gives the guardrails for handing one to engineering — directly reshapes the prototype-to-ship handoff.

picks.headline: My Actual AI Stack Right Now
picks.excerpt: A working designer walks through the exact AI tools he uses to design, code, edit video and run an agency — not predictions, the current stack and where each tool stops being useful.
picks.rationale: A practicing designer's real stack with the limits of each tool named — the fastest way to audit your own toolchain against someone shipping with it.
